title: Mihin and minne: answering with common into-forms
focus: Mihin and minne ask for a destination. Mihin sinä menet? — Menen kouluun.
targetSkills: Mihin and minne: answering with common into-forms

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Where are you going?”  Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. The illative is an into/to form; mihin aikaan uses that form in a time expression. Mihin and minne ask for a destination. Both can mean where to. These examples use a bounded set of common illatives, the forms meaning into a place: kouluun, taloon, kahvilaan and kirjastoon. The complete question means “Where are you going”.
requiredSkills: Mihin and minne: answering with common into-forms
exercises.targetSkill: Mihin and minne: answering with common into-forms

parts.formation: Mihin is the illative question form; in mihin aikaan it instead asks at what time.
